subject.title: Support multiple gateway tokens for multi-user session isolation

question: Should OpenClaw add native Gateway token-mode per-user principals for Control UI/WebChat session isolation, or keep per-user auth outside token mode through trusted-proxy/front-layer patterns such as Pinchy?
rationale: The issue changes a public credential, identity, authorization, and config boundary; code inspection proves the capability gap, but the permanent threat model and composition with scoped-token and author-attribution proposals require maintainer intent.

options.title: Design native Gateway token principals
options.body: Add a first-class token registry/principal model in Gateway auth and make it compose with scopes, session identity, SecretRef, revocation, audit logs, and docs.

options.title: Keep per-user auth at the front layer
options.body: Document trusted-proxy and Pinchy-style web frontends as the supported multi-user path and leave gateway.auth.token as a single operator secret.

options.title: Merge into scoped-token design
options.body: Treat this as a requirement on the broader scoped-token work in #92367, with per-user Control UI identity and session binding in the same principal model.

recommendation.title: Design native Gateway token principals
recommendation.body: Add a first-class token registry/principal model in Gateway auth and make it compose with scopes, session identity, SecretRef, revocation, audit logs, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the identity-bearing trusted-proxy auth mode that is the closest current alternative and are a strong routing owner for the auth-boundary decision.
